sources.finding: Snapshots persist on the sandbox's own filesystem and are tied to its lifecycle. For data that must outlive the sandbox entirely, Vercel directs users to Vercel Drive.

A Drive has a lifecycle independent from any sandbox. Deleting a sandbox leaves mounted Drive contents untouched; a later sandbox can mount the same Drive. The same guide states deleting a sandbox deletes its snapshots.
Vercel Drives are persistent attachable storage with sandbox-independent lifecycle and currently require the beta Sandbox SDK/CLI plus private-beta access.

why_the_earlier_receipts_were_wrong: The earlier reading conflated snapshot retention/expiry and separate snapshot resource operations with independence from the producing Sandbox. The June 29 provider guidance explicitly resolves that ambiguity in the opposite direction.

independent_source_fixes_that_remain_val.finding: These handlers were changed from stale networkPolicy {allow: domains} to the documented custom policy shape {mode:'custom', allowedDomains, allowedCIDRs, deniedCIDRs}; this is independent of Tier2 storage-carrier selection and remains source-only until executed.
